chunks.arabic_text: ٩ - سُهَيْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ، أَبُوك يَحْيَى، الْوَاسِطِيُّ، وَأُمُّهُ بِنْتُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ، أَبُوك جَعْفَرٍ الْأَحْوَلُ، مُؤْمِنُ الطَّاقِ. حَدِيثُهُ يُعْرَفُ تُورَةً، وَيُنْكَرُ أُخْرَى، وَيُجَازُ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ شَاهِدًا.

translations.en: 9 – Suhayl ibn Ziyad, Abu Yahya, al-Wasiti. His mother was the daughter of Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man, Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal, Mu'min al-Taq. His hadith is recognized sometimes, and rejected other times, and it is permissible to use him as a witness (for supporting evidence).

en.summary: This entry from Al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Du‘afā* highlights the nuanced evaluation of Suhayl ibn Ziyād al-Wāsiṭī, whose reliability fluctuates between acceptance and rejection, rendering him suitable primarily as a supporting witness (*shahid*) rather than an independent authority. His maternal lineage connects him to the prominent Ahl al-Bayt figure Abu Ja‘far al-Aḥwal, known as the 'Believer of the Chamber,' which adds a layer of familial prestige to his scholarly standing. This classification reflects the Shia tradition of *al-jarḥ wa al-ta‘dīl*, where narrators are often graded based on the consistency of their transmission across different contexts.
en.seo_question: What is the reliability status of Suhayl ibn Ziyad in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.سُهَيْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ: Suhayl ibn Ziyad, the narrator being assessed
key_terms.الْأَحْوَلُ: Al-Ahwal, a kunya/nickname meaning 'the squint-eyed' or 'one eye smaller than the other'
key_terms.مُؤْمِنُ الطَّاقِ: Mu'min al-Taq, a title meaning 'Believer of the Vault/Arch', often associated with a specific location or status
